article.dek: Parsons is active for his debut, Jacobs and Franklin are out, Walker is out for Thursday — and the evening board still hasn't flipped to Week 12, so Check is how you get a verdict on your book's number.

items.headline: Parsons is active — his debut is tonight
paragraphs: Micah Parsons is officially active for Green Bay, so his season debut is happening tonight against the Rams at SoFi Stadium, 8:00 p.m. ET kickoff. The Packers activated him from the physically unable to perform list on Tuesday after he was medically cleared following ACL surgery.
He has not played in 11 months, so expect a limited role, not a full night. A snap count is the likely plan for his first game back.
items.takeaway: Parsons is officially active and making his season debut tonight, likely on a snap count after 11 months out.

items.headline: Jacobs is out, and Franklin is a surprise scratch
paragraphs: Josh Jacobs is inactive tonight, as expected. He is only 12 days removed from surgery to repair a broken finger, and Kaleb Johnson leads the backfield in his place.

The surprise is linebacker Zaire Franklin. He practiced all week and looked set to return after four games out, but the Packers made him inactive with a shin injury, so he misses a fifth straight game. On the good side for Green Bay, center Sean Rhyan and guard Kevin Zeitler are both active after missing time.

The Rams had no surprises. Guard Steve Avila and center Coleman Shelton are out, as ruled out earlier in the week, along with tight end Terrance Ferguson. Puka Nacua and Davante Adams stay on injured reserve.
items.takeaway: Jacobs is out as expected and Kaleb Johnson leads the backfield. Franklin is a surprise scratch for a fifth straight game, while Rhyan and Zeitler are back. The Rams are out Avila and Shelton, as expected.

items.headline: Thursday flips: Walker is out, Ferguson is out
paragraphs: Kenneth Walker III is ruled out for Thursday night at Buffalo. That reverses the morning read — he practiced Tuesday and looked to be trending back, but the Chiefs ruled him out with a groin injury for a third straight game. Rookie Emmett Johnson starts again after back-to-back 100-yard games.

Dallas tight end Jake Ferguson is ruled out for Thursday against Philadelphia with knee and ankle injuries. That is a third straight missed game for him. The good news for Dallas is Dak Prescott was removed from the injury report and is healthy for Thursday.
Joe Milton III starts again Thursday for Philadelphia with Jalen Hurts out for the season. Kansas City also ruled out tackle Jaylon Moore, and tight end Noah Gray is questionable.
items.takeaway: Walker is out for Thursday after all, and Johnson starts again. Ferguson is out for Dallas, Prescott is healthy, and Milton starts again for Philadelphia.

items.headline: Rain and wind still on for Thursday night in Buffalo
paragraphs: Kansas City at Buffalo, Thursday night, 8:20 p.m. ET at Highmark Stadium: rain likely through the day and night, near 37 to 39 degrees, wind around 18 to 19 mph.
The other three games this week are indoors: Rams-Packers at SoFi Stadium, Bears-Lions at Ford Field, and Eagles-Cowboys at AT&T Stadium.
items.takeaway: Thursday night in Buffalo: rain likely all day and night, near 37 to 39 degrees, wind around 18 to 19 mph. The Rams-Packers, Bears-Lions and Eagles-Cowboys games are all indoors.

items.headline: The evening board still hasn't flipped to Week 12 — no cards yet
paragraphs: The board still shows Week 11 tonight, with all three headline cards — Hit Rate, Balanced, and Value — showing no play. Tonight's Packers-Rams game is not on the board at all, so there are no model numbers for tonight or for Thursday in the app.

Check the morning board for the first Week 12 lines. Meanwhile, the way to get a verdict on your book's number is Check: type in your book's line and price and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator.
items.takeaway: No Week 12 cards tonight because the board still shows Week 11 with empty headline cards, and tonight's game isn't on it at all. Check the morning board, and use Check on your own book's numbers in the meantime.

items.headline: The board doesn't know about tonight's inactives yet — your book might
paragraphs: The app's numbers were built before today's news, so they don't reflect Parsons' return, Jacobs being out, or Franklin's surprise scratch. Your book's line already has: the Rams have moved from -3.5 to -2.5 toward Green Bay.
That gap is exactly what Check is for. Put your book's price in and let the app re-evaluate it instead of guessing whether the move went too far.
items.takeaway: The app has not picked up today's news yet, so a line at your book may already reflect it. Run your book's number through Check rather than waiting for the board to catch up.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Handle: the money, not just the bets
paragraphs: Handle is the total money wagered on a side. It is different from the ticket count, which just counts how many bets were placed. A side can have fewer tickets but more handle, which means the average bet on that side is bigger.

Hypothetical example: imagine 100 tickets on the favorite and 100 tickets on the underdog, an even split by tickets. But the favorite's tickets add up to $1,000 while the underdog's add up to $4,000. Same number of bets, very different handle — the underdog is drawing the bigger money, even though the crowd looks evenly split.
items.takeaway: Tickets count heads, handle counts dollars — when the two disagree, the money side is usually the one drawing the bigger bets.

items.headline: Rams-Packers held at -2.5, and the total kept sliding
paragraphs: The Rams opened -3.5 and now sit at -2.5, a move toward Green Bay that lines up with Parsons' return being priced in. That number has held through the day: DraftKings still lists the Rams at -2.5 tonight, with the Packers at +116 on the moneyline.
The total has kept moving down. It opened around 46.5 and now sits at 44.5 at DraftKings, with some books at 43.5. The under was hit early in the week and the number has not come back.
The app has no Week 12 numbers yet, so none of this movement is app-tracked — it is reported movement from the wider market, and the app has nothing to compare it against until the board flips.

The betting splits line up with the move rather than fighting it. Most tickets and most of the money are on the same sides — the Rams on the spread, the Packers on the moneyline, the over on the total — so there is no public-versus-sharp split to fade tonight. If your book's number is different from the ones above, run it through Check and let the app give you a verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: Rams-Packers held at -2.5 after opening -3.5, and the total slid from 46.5 to 44.5. The splits agree with the move, so there is no split to fade — run your book's number through Check.

items.headline: Thursday is a Check day — and log tonight honestly
paragraphs: Tonight's game kicked off at 8:00 p.m. ET, so the inactives are final and there is nothing left to wait on there. For Thursday, the final word on who plays comes with inactives about 90 minutes before each kickoff, so check that before you lock anything in.
If your book has a Thursday number you like, type it into Check and let the app run it back through the model and evaluator. That is the verdict for your price, not a guess.
One more thing: settlement is manual, and the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself. Log tonight's result either way — the losers too.
items.takeaway: Tonight is decided, so look to Thursday: wait for inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff, run your book's number through Check, and log tonight's result honestly either way.
